programme: TP73 (p53-family factor transactivating CDKN1A, CDKN2A, CDKN2B, GADD45A, BAX, CCNE1, CDC25C) anchors a p53/Rb–CDKN1A/CDKN2A cell-cycle-checkpoint and senescence module. VENTX and HES4 converge on the same CDKN1A/CDKN2A/RB1 node from the homeobox and Notch-effector side; TBPL1 co-targets TP53, PCNA, WEE1, POT1 and TERF1, tying the checkpoint to DNA-damage and telomere control; DNMT1 is the epigenetic arm that can silence these same genes (TP53, RB1, PCNA) by promoter methylation and, in its Alzheimer's-linked target set, also methylates PSEN1; CDX1's targets (PCNA, CCND1, BCL2, VDR) sit on the same arrest/apoptosis node, though nothing in the record explains why an intestinal-identity factor would be recruited here.
role_in_a: In neurons, this checkpoint/senescence circuitry is the machinery invoked by the cell-cycle-re-entry model of neurodegeneration: post-mitotic neurons that ectopically re-express cell-cycle drivers (the CCNE1/CDC25C/GADD45A axis under TP73) and fail to complete division undergo apoptosis or senescence rather than division, and DNMT1-mediated methylation of PSEN1 has been proposed as a route to altered amyloidogenic processing.
role_in_b: In endometrial carcinoma, loss of the TP53/RB1/CDKN2A checkpoint is a defining molecular lesion (most sharply in the copy-number-high/serous-like subtype), and DNMT1-driven promoter hypermethylation silencing tumor suppressors (documented here for CDO1 via DNMT1, PMID 39159808) is an established route to checkpoint bypass in the endometrioid subtype.
shared_axis: Both a quiescent post-mitotic tissue (neurons) and a hormonally cycling proliferative tissue (endometrium) depend on the same TP53-family/Rb/CDKN1A-CDKN2A checkpoint to keep proliferation and apoptosis in balance; the same DNMT1-controlled methylation of that node would produce opposite phenotypes — ectopic cell-cycle re-entry and death in neurons, unchecked proliferation in endometrial epithelium — depending on which side of the checkpoint fails.
reasoning: DNMT1 is independently and mechanistically placed in both diseases by the retrieved literature, and TP73/VENTX/HES4/TBPL1 target sets are internally consistent with a single p53/Rb checkpoint module, so the programme is nameable and partially anchored in the record. But the disease-to-disease connection itself is not documented anywhere retrieved — it follows from reasoning about known checkpoint biology in each disease separately — and the one paper addressing TP73 in Alzheimer's disease actually reports no association, and CDX1 carries no supporting literature at all despite carrying the strongest recurrence (48/48), which caps the strength at moderate rather than strong.
support: PMID 38551404 (DNMT1 promoter methylation mechanism in Alzheimer's disease, via lncRNA SNHG1); PMID 42329254 and 39456478 (DNMT1-relevant neuroprotection/senescence contexts in Alzheimer's disease models); PMID 39159808 (DNMT1 promotes CDO1 promoter methylation in endometrial cancer, direct checkpoint-silencing mechanism); PMID 34439147 (PPARγ-DNMT1 interaction in a cancer-relevant epigenetic context, endometrial-cancer-adjacent); PMID 23414597 (tested and found no TP73-Alzheimer's association in mouse or human cohorts — cited as a caveat against the TP73 arm, not as support).
how_to_falsify: Run DNMT1 ChIP-seq/CUT&RUN and pharmacological DNMT1 inhibition (e.g., decitabine) in parallel in an AD-relevant neuronal model (iPSC neurons or post-mortem tissue) and an endometrial carcinoma cell line: if DNMT1 does not occupy or does not control methylation at CDKN2A/RB1/TP53 (and PSEN1 in the neuronal model) in both systems, the shared-epigenetic-checkpoint claim fails. Separately, CRISPR knockout of TP73 in an AD neuronal model with no change in CDKN1A/GADD45A/BAX expression would corroborate PMID 23414597's negative finding and remove TP73 from the AD side of the story entirely.
caveats: Cross-tissue comparison (brain vs. uterine endometrium) built from only 3 independent cohort pairs generating 48 patient-group comparisons, so the comparisons are not 48 independent data points. TP73's only disease-specific paper found no Alzheimer's association, weakening that arm of the module. CDX1, VENTX, HES4 and TBPL1 have zero disease-specific literature support despite high recurrence — their inclusion rests on target-set logic alone. POU2F1, LMO4, PAX2 and HOXB4 were left out of this programme because their evidence and target sets point to separate axes (immune/cholesterol signaling, synaptic biomarker status, and Müllerian/genitourinary developmental identity respectively), not the checkpoint module. SOX10 was excluded as tissue-generic despite high recurrence (0.75), so it is absent by design, not oversight.
